Balanced but cautious, with the hawkish tilt moderated by financial-stability considerations. The FOMC held the policy rate at 5.25–5.50% and reiterated the need for “greater confidence” in disinflation before cutting, but it also slowed the pace of Treasury redemptions—a dovish technical adjustment.

FSR lens: The Financial Stability Report flags ongoing vulnerabilities—CRE and office-sector stress (vacancy rates, credit quality pressure), structural vulnerabilities in money market funds, concentrated hedge fund activity in Treasury futures/market intermediation, elevated interest rate volatility, and high public debt amid geopolitical risks. These factors argue for risk-management caution (less appetite for additional tightening and a tempered balance sheet runoff) even as persistent inflation keeps policy restrictive.

Net tone: near-neutral with a slight hawkish bias, softer than before once FSR risks are incorporated.
